title: Mario Fanats, the best bass player
summary: He praises Fanats, a big man whose upright horn sounded like a bass fiddle, and talks about his sons.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: Do you remember who any of the outstanding bass players were?
No. Fanats. The Italian fella by the name of Fanats. Mario. Mario Fanats. He was about the best. Uh huh.
We know his sons. You do?
I was talking to his son last night.
Well, at least daddy was about the best.
We'll have to play this for him.

blocks.s: Mrs. Joe Loyacano (wife of Joe Loyacano)
blocks.x: His sons are about as, each about as wide as that sofa. Oh God. They run a, well I mean they're great big guys. Yeah.
Yeah. Well, Fanats was a big man himself, you know.

blocks.s: Mrs. Joe Loyacano (wife of Joe Loyacano)
blocks.x: They run a tobacco service on Decatur Street, you know, for cigarette machines.

Yeah. Yeah. Well, Fanats was a big heavy set man himself. Uh huh. But he blew a sousaphone and it sounded like a bass fiddle. Right. But he not a sousaphone but upright bass. It sounded just like a, man I remember one night, he come and we had a four piece job. In a house, a house party. And they sent him on bass. They come in there with this big bass horn. Jesus Christ, what are you gonna do in here? You blow the walls off this place. Don't worry, everything will be alright. He said, don't worry about nothing. So we start the play. Man, it sounded just like a bass fiddle. You couldn't tell whether it was a bass fiddle or a sousaphone.
Uh, who did he work with? Oh, Fanats?
Uh huh. He worked with anybody. Anybody at home. Oh yeah.
I just thought you might remember some special bands. Tip
